title: Catalog Compass
disclosure: Edited walkthrough using real application captures and real local inference. Synthetic English narration. Fictional supplier data.

scenes.title: Review supplier CSVs before import
captions: Catalog Compass helps freelancers review supplier product files before import.
It finds missing prices, duplicate product codes, and conflicting records, while keeping the original file unchanged.

scenes.title: A real open model runs locally
captions: This demo uses Qwen 3, a small open-weight model, through llama.cpp on this computer.
Local mode needs no API key. Setup and startup are available from AI settings.

scenes.title: Load a file and match its columns
captions: We load the included sample: ten fictional products with unfamiliar column names.
SKU, product name, and regular price are required. The other fields are optional.

scenes.title: AI suggests the meaning of each column
captions: The model suggests Item ref for SKU, Display label for name, and List amount for price.
It receives column headers and a few short example values, not the full catalog.

scenes.title: A model mistake becomes a review task
captions: Here is a real mistake: the model used Kind for both Product type and Description.
The app clears both choices and explains exactly which column and fields conflict.

scenes.title: The reviewer resolves the conflict
captions: I select Kind as Product type and leave Description unselected.
The warning disappears. Barcode remains matched to GTIN, separately from the supplier's internal SKU.

scenes.title: Confirm before checking
captions: After reviewing the selections, I confirm the mapping and run the checks.
Python rules check the values. The model does not invent prices or delete duplicates.

scenes.title: See the rows that need attention
captions: For this sample, the reviewed mapping produces four errors and six warnings across nine rows.
These are fixture results, not an estimate of real-world accuracy.

scenes.title: Inspect conflicting source values
captions: One product code appears with prices of thirty-two and thirty-nine dollars.
The report shows both source rows, so the reviewer can ask the supplier which price is correct.

scenes.title: Download a report for the handoff
captions: Download the issue report or a mapped CSV for further review.
Problem rows are preserved. This is a review tool, not an automatic store importer.

scenes.title: Or connect a compatible API
captions: An optional API mode avoids the local-model download. Enter your provider, model, and key, then test the connection.
Samples go to that provider. The key stays in memory and is cleared when you refresh.

scenes.title: A small tool for a concrete service
captions: The service to test is simple: review one supplier file and deliver a useful exception report.
Forty-four automated tests pass. Paid demand remains unvalidated. The next step is a supervised freelancer trial.
